speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are not an add-on to our economy.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are the invisible workforce behind our workforce.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: That is why MDWs are not just a labour issue.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are a critical backbone of Singapore's care economy.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In my Punggol constituency, I met a mother in her early 40s.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She had two young children and she came to see me as there was an issue with processing her MDW's entry into Singapore.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She shared that her father had just been diagnosed with early dementia.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And she told me quietly, "Without my helper, I will have to resign.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Please help me." This is the reality for thousands of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: If we want women to stay in the workforce, if we want families to remain financially stable and if we want our seniors to age with dignity, then we must get home caregiving right.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Care does not fail because families do not care.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: When employers and MDWs understand each other, seniors are safer, children are calmer, families are stable and workers are treated with dignity.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: But when communication fails, when expectations are unclear, when skills are missing, that is when things unravel and plans fall apart.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Indeed, I believe that our Singapore employers intrinsically care about their helpers, or "aunties", as we affectionally call our MDWs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: A few seasons ago, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) started on a series of "Meet-the-Members Sessions", our labour version of the regular Meet-the-People Sessions that Members of Parliament (MPs) conduct.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Members could speak with us on grievances in the workplace, unfairness and harassment issues.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I had prepared myself on fronting these thorny issues, but I was surprised.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In the weeks that I was the attending labour MP, the majority of our members who came to see me were MDW employers, sharing with me the issues that they had with their helpers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Perhaps, it was because I am the only female labour MP, the sharing was passionate, but the issues were common across all who came.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I was impressed and heart-warmed and indeed, inspired by how the sharing was not focused on complaints of MDW behaviours and strained relations but on how the Labour Movement could give practical tips and know-how on managing and improving MDW and employer relations.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It has been a while now, but I still recall how Mdm E, not her real name, a lady in her 50s, told me that after years of hiring helpers in their late-40s who were married with children, she was now the employer of a helper in her early-20s, who is single and carefree.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And she had cheerfully quipped that she realised, in the same way that her children are called "strawberries", that there is also now a generation of "strawberry helpers".

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And in her careful observations, there are many differences in working well with the many different generations of helpers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And the differences show in many everyday practices, for example, the use of handphones, personal spaces, sleeping hours and indeed, the use of social media.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In fact, the majority of the members who came to see me were like Mdm E.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And this inspired the NTUC Woman and Family Unit to evolve these clinics and sessions into a series of highly-attended events, called "POW-WOW: Power of Women WOW".

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: These sessions brought employers together with their MDWs to better access resources and strengthen relations.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Indeed, during these sessions, our partners also organised an award ceremony for exemplary employer-MDW pairs, some working together for more than half their lives.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: These events are very well attended and our partnerships well covered, from non-governmental organisations, like the Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE); trade associations, like the Association for Employment Agencies (Singapore); to Government departments, like the Ministry of Manpower (MOM); to private firms like Singtel and DBS.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: These events demonstrate the openness and desire of Singapore families and their helpers to strengthen their relationships, and the many parties coming forward to offer resources to co-create possibilities, safe spaces and ecosystems for MDW-employer relations to flourish.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They need certainty that care and trust will hold.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: The need for care is ever-growing, the will for better partnerships is strong and vast resources are available.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I believe we can organise better to strengthen support and dignity for MDWs and our Singapore families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And that is what my proposals today are about.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Care today is not just only about housekeeping.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It is about dementia care, post-hospital recovery, disability support, child development and senior well-being.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Currently, the NTUC's CDE has partnered with the Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan Cultural Academy and The Salvation Army to run conversational Hokkien and Cantonese language classes for our MDWs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This has been helpful in building strong bridges between our MDWs and their families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Because when an MDW cannot understand a senior, care becomes unsafe.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Language is not just a "nice to have".

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: If a grandma in her 80s cannot tell her caregiver that she is in pain, we will have all failed her in her care needs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In my Meet-the-People Sessions, I have met many first-time employers who did not even know where to seek help when their MDW plans fail.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They relied on their employment agency and many got it wrong.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Take, Ms T, not her real name, for example.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She came to see me as she was in a bind.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She could not get along with her helper and the language barrier caused deep rifts in everyday handling of chores.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She had a young child and was also worried about her child's safety as her helper had different standards when it came to safety and care.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She sought the help of her employment agent but was told that there were no replacements available and if she insisted on having the agent take back the helper, she would need to pay an extra fee.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This was not in the contract that she signed and she was actually covered for one free replacement.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Not wanting to pay the additional fee, she forced herself to continue with the helper.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In the end, they both got into a physical fight.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It ended up being a viral clip, traumatising both my resident and her family and indeed, the helper.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This was not a good outcome for all involved and I felt that the employment agency could have stepped in to play a larger role in mitigating.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Luckily, with an appeal, our friends from the Association for Employment Agencies (Singapore) stepped in and helped both the helper and my resident out of this situation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This is for families with frail seniors, special needs children or medical needs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Matching can be done by trained care assessors, not sales staff.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: A wrong match does not just only cost money; it can break a family and deeply hurt our workers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Our PCP for migrant workers could be a model worth studying as they afford primary healthcare for workers with low co-payments.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This could encourage early care-seeking and can worsen health outcomes.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Could the Government then consider a similar outpatient primary care scheme for MDWs?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Even a modest co-payment structure for routine outpatient visits could prevent small ailments from becoming serious, thereby protecting worker welfare and reducing family anxieties.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Mr and Mrs T first came to see me at my Meet-the-People Session, looking both concerned and actually a little guilty.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They shared that they are thinking of sending back their helper who has been with them for over 20 years.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She has almost become family but as she was struck with cancer and required surgery and treatment, Mr and Mrs T, as retirees, were unable to afford the out-of-pocket expenses for this.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: With their appeals for subsidised medical fees rejected, the family had to send their helper home, feeling guilty that they could have made a difference since the cancer was caught early.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Ms W's experience caused her to fall into some financial duress.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Her helper was with her for only one year, when she suddenly developed a fever and body aches.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Her oxygen levels were dangerously low and Ms W had to rush her to the hospital.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: After several rounds of checks, her helper's condition remained undiagnosable and finally, she was certified unfit to work and was sent back to her home country.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This entire episode caused Ms W to go past her insurance thresholds and, with the 25% co-payment, she had to pay a high five-digit sum out of pocket.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As such, would MOM consider getting employment agencies to be clearer on their advisories to employers on the medical and hospitalisation responsibilities for their helpers?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As healthcare costs increase in Singapore, too, to mandate timely reviews of insurance coverage and co-payment levels, so that our Singapore families are adequately supported when their helpers need medical and hospitalisation care.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Healthy caregivers mean stable families and we need to re-focus mental health into our system.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Unlike regular employees, many MDWs live relatively isolated lives, have no colleagues in the workplace and while living with families and their employers, they are separated hundreds of miles from their own families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Some are caring for sick parents back home via proxies and monthly transfers home while caring for ours here.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I welcome ground-up initiatives, like the Association for Employment Agencies (Singapore) partnering with The RICE Company, to provide recreational and social integration activities, and NTUC's CDE interviewing first-time MDWs within their first six months.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: To close the circle, our Singaporean families must also be encouraged to be stakeholders in this, as the care ecosystem can only be complete with our families as participants and beneficiaries alike.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Some need backup support beyond the traditional live-in arrangement and yet, others guard privacy above everything else, preferring a few hours of help for just a few days in a week.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Building on schemes, like the Household Services Scheme, could we pilot care-focused extensions – part-time carers who are properly trained and fairly contracted or pooling arrangements where several families can share a trained worker on a regulated basis?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Such models could serve our working parents, those with intermittent caregiving needs and families who cannot yet afford or require full-time live-in help.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Let us fix our levy rules for real caregiving burdens.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Today, levy concessions are based largely on age as well as people with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Caregiver burden is heavier when family's needs are complex.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Residents have asked about levy concessions and targeted financial support related to hiring an MDW.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Consider single mothers or fathers with special needs kids who are also caring for their senior parents.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Consider families where both parents work full-time to make ends meet.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This should include supervision-intensive but non-Activity for Daily Living (ADL) cases, such as early dementia, as well as youths above 16, frail adults aged 60 to 66, moderate dependency cases and families with multiple dependents that require care support.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Because, really, being a single mother caring for a disabled teen and an elderly parent must feel supported as she loves and cares for her family.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: If we want Singapore to remain strong in an ageing world, we must invest in the people who keep our homes running.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: By strengthening training and communication, uplifting employment agencies, improving healthcare coverage, exploring flexible care models and refining support for families with heavier caregiving burdens, we can build a caregiving ecosystem that is fair, resilient and sustainable for both Singaporean families and the MDWs who support them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: In my response, I will cover three key aspects of how the Government is addressing these issues: first, measures to support MDWs in performing their caregiving duties, such as training and alternative care options by the Government; second, measures to support MDW employers in accessing affordable care services; and third, measures to strengthen MDW employers' working relationships with their MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This is driven by various factors including demographic, social and economic changes: more elderly Singaporeans requiring care, as well as more dual-income families with less extended family support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: I share the Member's view that MDWs play an important role in supporting households with different caregiving needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Their dedication to caring for the young and elderly in our homes are invaluable to many families in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Hence, we had introduced various measures in the last five years to support MDWs' well-being, such as having mandatory rest days, as well as interviews in the first year of employment to check that they are settling in well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: These measures demonstrate our commitment towards improving employment conditions for MDWs, in line with international standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: With increasing numbers of MDWs providing care to the elderly, we agree with the Member that training is important to enable them to provide quality care on a sustained basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Both family caregivers and their MDWs may tap on the Caregivers Training Grant (CTG) to offset the costs of attending caregiver training courses organised by approved providers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To support caregivers' training needs, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) offers over 240 courses covering a range of caregiving training skills, which address the caregiving needs cited by the Member, namely dementia, elder disability and post-hospitalisation care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Home-based training is also available for caregivers to learn how to provide home-based care for their care recipients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We agree with the Member that language skills by caregivers are important to communicate effectively with their care recipients, especially for MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: As mentioned by the Member, employers or MDWs can tap on courses offered by the CDE, the Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan Cultural Academy and The Salvation Army for basic conversational Hokkien and Cantonese courses respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Non-profit organisations, such as the Archdiocesan Commission for the Pastoral Care of Migrants and Itinerant People, Brahm Centre and Aidha also conduct English and Mandarin courses for MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: I also agree with the Member, that it is important to support the mental health of MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Employers must provide at least one rest day per month, that cannot be compensated away, to allow MDWs to form support networks outside of the household.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOM has a dedicated helpline with native speakers for MDWs in distress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We also partner with CDE, Alliance for Domestic Employees Outreach and Brahm Centre to provide psychological first-aid training, counselling and recreational activities for MDWs to improve their mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Even as we strengthen MDW's caregiver support on training and mental health, we should recognise that care needs and family circumstances are diverse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: As the Member has rightfully pointed out in her speech, live-in MDWs may not be the best care option for every household and we need to provide more alternatives that are better fit-for-purpose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Therefore, the Government has been working with the industry to offer a wider range of full-time and part-time eldercare and domestic services that are accessible and affordable for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: In lieu of relying on a live-in MDW, alternative care options such as the recently mainstreamed Shared Stay-in Senior Caregiving Services and the upcoming Home Personal Care enhancements, can help to support seniors with their activities of daily living.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Households that require part-time or ad hoc help with household chores can consider engaging companies on the Household Services Scheme (HSS) instead of hiring an MDW.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Since formalising the HSS as a permanent scheme in 2021, the number of HSS companies has increased from about 80 to 240 today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Member also highlighted affordability challenges that MDW employers may face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: First, we have the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) that currently provides cash payouts of up to $400 per month to support those who are being cared for at home and require permanent assistance with at least three ADLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The enhancements to HCG will take effect from April 2026.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Currently, around 72% of households hiring MDWs already benefit from the levy concession as they have either a child below 16 years old; or an elderly person at least 67 years old; or a person with disabilities living in the household.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Regardless of age or impairment type, persons who require assistance permanently to perform at least one ADL, would qualify for the Levy Concession.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This includes persons with dementia or who have special needs, who may physically be able to perform the ADL, but require assistance or supervision to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To better protect employers from high unexpected medical bills, MOM regularly reviews the coverage of medical insurance policies for MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Employers who prefer greater coverage can choose to purchase more comprehensive insurance plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: On the Member's suggestion to extend the PCP to MDWs, I will highlight that the objective of the PCP is to provide migrant workers with accessible primary healthcare, including setting up of migrant worker medical centres near dormitories, and to strengthen public health resilience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The medical centres for PCP are, thus, largely located near migrant worker dormitories, which are in areas generally not adequately served by existing medical facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Employers of MDWs who prefer cost predictability of primary care may consider purchasing more comprehensive insurance claims without patient coverage on a voluntary basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: I agree with the Member that employment agencies play an important role in the relationship between employers and MDW.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ensuring a good match between employers and MDWs can help to provide a good start in the working relationship.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOM has put in place process to regulate employment agencies and facilitate better matching of employers and MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: First, employment agencies are required to comply with MOM's regulations and guidelines to ensure that they are professional in their dealings with their clients, both the employers and the MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Employers may use the FDW eService portal to access information about MDWs' past work performance, length of each employment and reasons why MDW have left their past employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Thirdly, MOM provides an online employment agency directory to provide information to households looking to engage an employment agency's service, including the employment agencies' customer service ratings, years of experience, retention and transfer rates of their MDWs emplaced.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The directory improves transparency by allowing employers to engage the employment agencies that best meet their needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Lastly, MOM has an education and outreach programme for both employers and MDWs to align expectations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: First-time employers are required to attend the Employers' Orientation Programme, which educates employers on their responsibilities of care towards their MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MDWs, in turn, must go through the Settling-in Programme which educates them on avenues to seek help when needed, on how to manage their own stress and communicate effectively with their employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This further helps to foster a harmonious relationship between employers and their MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Government has been expanding caregiving options and ensuring they remain accessible and affordable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: We will continue to find ways to safeguard the interests of MDW employers while protecting the well-being of MDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: It takes a many-hands approach to create an ecosystem of support for MDWs and their employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Our employment agencies, Association of Employment Agencies, CDE, the NTUC and non-governmental organisations play an important role in fostering harmonious relationships between MDWs and their employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Let us continue to work together to sustain this ecosystem of support for MDWs and employers, and foster a culture of mutual understanding and respect within the community.
